areas.name: Sign-in and account
areas.intro: Signing in with a password and a second step, refreshing and ending sessions, two-step verification and passkeys. Browser flows; automation uses API tokens.

routes.summary: Signs in with `email` and `password`. Returns an access token and sets the refresh cookie, or answers `mfa_required` (with `mfa_token`) or `password_change_required`. 429 when rate-limited.
Completes sign-in with the `mfa_token` and exactly one of `code` (TOTP or recovery code) or `credential` (passkey assertion); 422 otherwise. Returns an access token and the refresh cookie.
Passkey challenge for the second sign-in step (after the password).
routes.exempt: issues a single-use passkey challenge only; the answer is audited by /auth/mfa (login.succeeded or mfa.failed)

routes.summary: A new access token from the refresh cookie (rotating it). Requires the `X-Requested-With: procera` header (403 without it); 401 without a valid cookie.
routes.exempt: rotation on every session renewal; reuse is audited as security.token_reuse and sign-in as login.succeeded

routes.summary: Ends the session behind the refresh cookie and clears it; 204. Requires the `X-Requested-With: procera` header.
The signed-in user's account and the current token's facts (methods used, auth time, plane, workspace, expiry).
Revokes every session of the caller's account and invalidates its outstanding access tokens, then clears the refresh cookie; 204.
Starts authenticator-app enrolment and returns the secret to scan; confirm it with `POST /me/mfa/totp/confirm`.
Confirms TOTP enrolment with a `code`; returns the recovery codes (shown once) and an upgraded access token for this session.
The caller's registered passkeys.
Registers a passkey (`name`, `credential`) answering the challenge from `/me/mfa/webauthn/options`; 201. Recovery codes are returned once when it is the first second factor.
A WebAuthn registration challenge for adding a passkey.
routes.exempt: issues a single-use passkey challenge only; the registration is audited as mfa.webauthn_added

routes.summary: Removes one of the caller's passkeys; 204. Needs a sign-in within the last 5 minutes (401 `step_up_required`).

areas.name: Outgoing webhooks
areas.intro: Endpoints that receive signed events, their delivery log, replay, test events and secret rolling, and the event catalogue.

routes.summary: The event types a webhook can receive, with what each means.
The workspace's endpoints with their last delivery (`connector:view`).

A new endpoint (`url` https, `events` types or `["*"]`, `description`; `connector:configure`; at most 20). 201 with the endpoint and its `secret` (shown only here). 422 for a URL inside a private network or a port other than 443/80/8443/8080.
One endpoint (`connector:view`), with an `ETag` of its revision.
Changes the URL, events, description or on/off (`connector:configure`; honours `If-Match`). Turning an endpoint back on clears why it was turned off.
Removes an endpoint and its delivery log (`connector:configure`). 204.
A new signing secret (`connector:manage_secrets`); the previous one also signs for 24 hours. Returns `{secret, previous_valid_until}`.
Queues a `webhook.test` event for the endpoint (`connector:configure`); the next delivery pass sends it. 202 with the delivery.
The endpoint's deliveries, newest first (at most 200), each with its state, attempts, last status, error and duration, a response excerpt and the event body (`connector:view`).
Sends a delivery again from the start of its retry schedule, with the same event id (`connector:configure`).

areas.name: API tokens
areas.intro: Personal API tokens: create, list and revoke your own; security admins list and revoke everyone's.

routes.summary: My tokens in this workspace, newest first.
A new token with some of my own permissions; the secret is shown once.
Revoke one of my tokens (repeating it is a no-op).
Every token in the workspace (`api_token:manage`).
Revoke anyone's token (`api_token:manage`).

areas.name: Workspace and members
areas.intro: Your workspaces and permissions, switching workspace and step-up, invitations, members, deactivation and reactivation.

routes.summary: The workspaces I belong to, and which one my current token is for (`active`).
Issues an access token for the chosen workspace (or none, for the home view).
Re-authenticates within the current sign-in and returns an access token with a fresh `auth_time`.
Passkey challenge for step-up.
routes.exempt: issues a single-use passkey challenge only; the answer is audited by /session/step-up

routes.summary: Public: what the invitation page shows to the holder of the link.
Accepts an invitation (body `{token}`) for the signed-in user and returns the new `workspace_id` and `membership_id`.
Creates an account from an invitation (`token`, `display_name`, `password`) and joins the workspace; 201. Sign in afterwards to get a workspace token.
Every permission and the built-in role templates with their permissions.
My effective permissions in this workspace, and whether I manage a team (`manages`: I have direct reports or hold `work:view_team` on a department).
Every member of the workspace (`member:view`).
The workspace's invitations (`member:invite`). Links are never included.
Invites an email address with a set of `roles` (`member:invite`); 201. The invitation link is sent by email only and is never returned here.
Revokes a pending invitation so its link stops working (`member:invite`); 204.
A fresh one-time link for a pending invitation, for the inviter to hand over when email isn't set up. The earlier link stops working. Only this response carries the token; lists never do.
Deactivates a member, ending their access to the workspace (`member:deactivate`); 204.
Brings a deactivated member back with the roles they had. Restoring access is treated like granting it: step-up, and no restoring roles the caller could not grant.
The workspace's roles with their permissions (`role:view`).
A custom role (`key`, `name`, `permissions`, optional `cloned_from` template); `role:manage` plus a recent step-up (401 `step_up_required` otherwise); 201.
Replaces a role's `permissions` (`role:manage` plus a recent step-up); 204. The audit entry records what was added, removed and how many members it affects.
Shows what a role change would do before saving it.
routes.exempt: read-only impact preview; POST only because it carries a body

routes.summary: Role grants in the workspace, optionally for one `?membership_id=` (`role:view`).
Grants `role_key` to exactly one of `membership_id` or `group_id` (else 422), with an optional scope, `expires_at` and `reason`; `member:manage_roles` plus a recent step-up; 201 `{id}`.
Revokes a role grant (`member:manage_roles` plus a recent step-up); 204.

areas.name: Directory
areas.intro: Departments, groups, positions, managers and the CSV import that keeps them in step with your HR system.

routes.summary: Every department in the workspace (`directory:view`).
A new department (`name`, optional `parent_id`); `directory:manage`; 201.
Renames a department, moves it (`parent_id`, `null` for the root) or sets its head (`head_membership_id`); `directory:manage`; 204.
Deletes an empty department (`directory:manage`); 204. A department that still has sub-departments, members or positions is refused with 409.

What refers to a department, shown before deleting it: role grants scoped to it, and active or draft campaigns, announcements and policies whose audience names it. Titles only, and only for people who manage the directory.
Every group in the workspace (`directory:view`).
A new group (`name`, optional `description`); `directory:manage`; 201.
Deletes a group (`directory:manage`); 204.
The membership ids in a group (`directory:view`).
Adds a member (`membership_id`) to a group (`directory:manage`); 204.
Removes a member from a group (`directory:manage`); 204.
Every position in the workspace (`directory:view`).
Positions are off unless `directory.positions.enabled`.
The directory locations in use, with how many active members each has (audience pickers).
Deletes a position (`directory:manage`); 204.
Sets a member's directory fields (`title`, `department_id`, `manager_membership_id`, `location`; `null` clears one); `directory:manage`. Returns `{changed}`.
A member's directory fields, groups and resolved manager (explicit, department head or none); `directory:view`.

What a member holds, for the leaving flow (docs/design/ia-competitive-analysis.md §8.3): documents they own, drafts and reviews they started, campaigns they run, groups, direct reports, role grants and open acknowledgements, plus the workspace's hand-over default. Titles and counts only.
CSV directory import. `mode=plan` (default) reports what would change and rolls back; `mode=apply` commits.

areas.name: Library (SOPs and policies)
areas.intro: Controlled documents: drafts, review and approval, publishing as major or minor versions, retirement, review cadence, verification and change requests.

routes.summary: The SOPs and policies the caller may view, filtered by `kind`, `state` and `collection` (sub-collections included). Drafts and restricted ones show only to authors of the kind.
A new SOP or policy (`kind`, `key`, `title`, optional `criticality`, `content`) with its first draft (`<kind>:create`). 201 with the artifact and version; 409 `key_taken`.
One document, the versions the caller may see and `my_actions` (what the caller may do with it, scoped grants included). Returns an `ETag` of its revision.
Starts a new draft from the latest version's content (`<kind>:edit_draft`). 201; 409 when a draft or review is already open.
One version with its content and review state (`<kind>:view`; drafts only for authors of the kind). Returns an `ETag` of its revision.
Replaces a draft's `content` (`<kind>:edit_draft`). Send `If-Match: "<revision>"` to guard against overwrites (412 when stale); 409 when the version is not a draft.
Semantic diff between two versions of the same artifact: block-level added/removed/changed with word-level changes inside changed blocks.
Sets the document's review cadence in `days`, or `null` for the workspace default (`<kind>:publish`).
The owner confirms the published content is still correct, with an optional `comment`; a new review period starts now (`<kind>:publish`).
Verifying a controlled artifact needs a recent authentication, like approving it.
Removes the document's verification badge (`<kind>:approve`).
Change requests proposed for a document, optionally filtered by `state` (`<kind>:view`).
Proposes a change to a document with a `title` and optional `body`; any reader may (`<kind>:view`). 201.
One change request (`<kind>:view` on its document).
`decision` `accepted`, `declined` (needs a `resolution`) or `implemented` (needs a `version_id` of the same document); `<kind>:publish`. 409 from a wrong state.
Sets a document's `category`, who it applies to (`applicability` audience, `null` = everyone) and the `restricted` flag (`<kind>:publish`). 422 for an empty audience.
The policies that apply to the caller, with what changed since the previous version.
The collections the caller may see, or all of them with `collection:manage` (`collection:view`). `can_manage` says which.
A new collection with a `name`, optionally under `parent_id` (`collection:manage`). 201.
Renames a collection and/or moves it (and its subtree) under `parent_id` (`null` = top level); `collection:manage`. A collection cannot move under itself.
Deletes an empty collection (`collection:manage`). 204; 409 while it still holds documents or sub-collections.
Sets who may see a collection (`visibility` audience, `null` = everyone); `collection:manage`. 422 for an empty audience.
Filing a document needs `publish` on its kind (the people who control where it lives).
Changes a document's accountable owner to an active member (`membership_id`); `<kind>:publish`.
A document's RACI assignments (`<kind>:view`).
Replaces a document's RACI, with at most one accountable assignee (`<kind>:publish`).
RACI of every document the caller may see, as CSV. Audited.

A self-contained, print-ready HTML document (browsers print it as a tagged PDF), Markdown, or a Word document with real headings, lists and tables. Superseded and retired versions carry a "not the current version" banner. Audited.
Sends a draft for review (`<kind>:edit_draft`); when the workspace requires no review for it, it is approved at once.
Takes a version out of review back to draft (`<kind>:edit_draft`).
Records a `decision` (`approve`, `reject`, `changes_requested`; the last two need a `comment`). Authors cannot review their own (403); controlled approvals need step-up.
Publishes an approved version now or at `effective_at`, as a `major` or `minor` `change` (`<kind>:publish`; controlled needs step-up). `reack` says who must re-acknowledge.
What publishing a version would do: its number as a major or minor change, whether each asks for a re-acknowledgement, how many people that reaches and by when.
Retires a published or deprecated version with a `reason`; it is read-only afterwards (`<kind>:publish`).

areas.name: Acknowledgement campaigns
areas.intro: Ask people to acknowledge a published document by a deadline, with reminders, escalation to managers and evidence exports.

routes.summary: Every acknowledgement campaign in the workspace, optionally filtered by `?state=`. Needs `campaign:view`.
A draft campaign for a published SOP or policy version (`version_id`, `audience`, optional `title`, `due_at`, `audience_snapshot`, `ack_text`). Needs `campaign:manage`; 201.
One campaign with an `ETag`; a draft also carries `audience_preview`, the number of active members its audience reaches now. Needs `campaign:view`.
The campaign's assignments, optionally `?state=pending|completed|overdue` (422 otherwise). Needs `campaign:view`.
Evidence export as CSV. The export itself is audited (`campaign.evidence_exported`).
Launches a draft, snapshotting its audience into assignments and notifying every assignee. Needs `campaign:manage`; 409 unless it is a draft.
Closes an active campaign (optional `reason`), freezing it as evidence; open assignments stay as the record. Needs `campaign:manage`; 409 in any other state.
Cancels a draft or active campaign; a `reason` is required (422). Needs `campaign:manage`; 409 in any other state.
Sends a reminder now to every open assignment of active members and returns `{reminded}`. Needs `campaign:manage`; 409 unless the campaign is active.
The caller's own acknowledgements (`?state=pending|completed`; default: open and completed), limited to the kinds they may acknowledge.

Acknowledges the caller's own assignment, optionally checking `content_hash` (409 `content_changed`). 409 `already_acknowledged` on repeat; needs `sop:acknowledge` for SOPs or `policy:view` for policies (announcements are acknowledged on the announcement).

areas.name: Announcements
areas.intro: Official messages with audiences, approval before publishing, scheduling, read receipts and required acknowledgements.

routes.summary: Announcements the caller composes or decides on, optionally filtered by `?state=`; managers see all. Each item says whether publishing it `needs_approval`. Needs `announcement:create` or `announcement:publish`.
A new draft announcement (title, content, audience, priority, ack and timing fields). Needs `announcement:create`; 201 with an `ETag`. 409 when announcements are turned off.
The published, unexpired announcements sent to the caller, with read and acknowledgement receipts; `?unread=true` keeps only unread ones. Needs `announcement:view`.
One announcement the caller may see (author, publisher once submitted, or recipient), with an `ETag`. Anyone else gets 404.
Replaces a draft's content; author with `announcement:create`, or a manager. Optional `If-Match: "<revision>"` (412 if stale); 409 unless the announcement is a draft.
Sends the author's draft for approval; approvers are notified when the workspace's approval rule applies to its audience. 409 unless it is a draft.
Approves a pending announcement and publishes it now, or schedules it for `publish_at`. Needs `announcement:publish`; 403 `sod_violation` if the approver is the author.
Returns a pending announcement to draft with a required `comment` (422 if empty). Needs `announcement:publish`; 409 unless it is pending approval.
Publishes a draft now, or schedules it for its `publish_at`, when no approval applies (409 otherwise). Author holding `announcement:publish`, or a manager; 422 if expired.
Withdraws a scheduled or published announcement with a `reason` and closes its acknowledgement campaign. Needs `announcement:publish` or authorship; 409 otherwise.
Records that the caller read it (first read only; repeats change nothing) and returns the receipt. Needs `announcement:view`.
Acknowledges the announcement and completes the caller's campaign assignment with it: one acknowledgement, one audit record (`announcement.acknowledged`, citing the assignment).
Reach, read and acknowledgement counts, overall and by department. Author with `announcement:create`, or `announcement:manage`.

areas.name: Requests
areas.intro: Request types you may start, starting a request, your and all requests, request details with steps, timeline and why each step went to whom, comments and watching.

routes.summary: The request types the caller may start (enabled in this workspace, and the caller is in the type's audience), with their start forms priced in the workspace currency. `?scope=all` lists every built-in with `enabled` and `audience`, for Settings › Requests (`workspace:settings.view`).
Requests by `scope`: `mine` (default, `request:view_own`) or `all` (`request:view_all`), optionally filtered by `status`.
Starts a request of `type` with `input` answers (201, with `Location`). Requires an `Idempotency-Key` (a repeat replays the first response; 409 if reused for another body). Needs `request:start`.
"Who approves this" before sending (`request:start`): a dry run of the routing for the answers so far. A read: nothing is written, nothing is audited, the transaction rolls back.
routes.exempt: read-only dry run of the routing (who approves); POST only carries the draft answers, nothing is written

routes.summary: One request in full, plus `can_cancel` (whether you may cancel it). 404 unless you may see it (view-all, involved, or in your team).
Cancels an open request with a `reason`. Only the requester or a holder of `request:cancel`; 404 if you can't see it.
The conversation on a request (internal notes hidden from the requester) and its watchers.
Posts a comment (`request:comment` and able to see the request). Each mentioned member must be able to see the request too (422 on `/mentions` naming who can't). Audited `request.commented`.
Follows a request: new comments and its outcome reach the caller. Audited `request.watched`.
Stops following a request. Audited `request.unwatched`.

areas.name: My work
areas.intro: Your approvals, tasks and acknowledgements: decide, reassign and delegate work items, and team workload for managers.

routes.summary: Work items by `state`: `open` (default) and `done` are yours (`work:view_assigned`); `unassigned` and `overdue` are workspace-wide and need `work:reassign`.
Workload per person: `scope=team` (default) is the caller's reporting line, for a manager in the directory or `work:view_team`; `scope=all` is everyone and needs workspace oversight.
The open steps one person holds: visible for someone in the caller's reporting line, or anyone with workspace oversight. Others get 404.
Technical incidents: `monitoring:view_dashboards` or `request:retry`.
Runs an incident again (audited `incident.retried`, a reason required).
Gives up on an incident (audited `incident.dismissed`, a reason required).

Records your decision (`outcome`, `comment`, `fields`, `files`). Requires `If-Match` with the item's revision (428 without) and `work:complete`; 409 when already decided. An optional `Idempotency-Key` replays the first response.
Moves an open step to one member (admin oversight). `Idempotency-Key` optional: a replay of the same key returns the first answer.
Hands a step the caller holds to a colleague. Separation of duties is re-checked (422 `sod_excluded` on `/membership_id`); audited `work_item.delegated`.

areas.name: Processes (Guided Studio)
areas.intro: Design processes: templates, drafts saved with If-Match, validation in plain language, test runs, who a step will go to, and publishing.

routes.summary: Every process in the workspace, with its draft and published versions.
A new process with its first draft from a template.
A blank process and every built-in request type.
The problems publishing would report, in plain language.
routes.exempt: a read: compiles a draft against the workspace and returns its problems

routes.summary: What a draft does for these answers and choices, worked out in memory (nothing is stored, nobody is told).
routes.exempt: a read: simulates a draft in memory; nothing is stored or sent

routes.summary: Who each candidate of a step reaches in the directory today.
routes.exempt: a read: counts who a step's candidates reach in the directory

routes.summary: `GET /processes/{id}`.
`PUT /processes/{id}/draft` with `If-Match: "<revision>"`: saves the open draft, or opens a new draft from the published version first (then If-Match is not needed).
Submits the draft and, when no review is needed, publishes it. A process that does not compile is refused with its problems (422 `{problems}`).

areas.name: Out of office and delegation
areas.intro: Set and clear out of office, for yourself or (as an admin) someone else, with a delegate who decides on your behalf.

routes.summary: Your current out-of-office period and delegate, if any, and `can_set`: whether you may change it (`work:delegate` and the self-service setting). Membership only.
Sets your out-of-office from `starts_on` to `ends_on` (dates) with a `delegate` and optional `note`. Needs `work:delegate`; 403 when self-service is turned off.
Clears your out-of-office (204). Same checks as setting it.
Someone's out-of-office. Needs `work:delegate` and either `work:reassign` over that person or being their manager; 404 if they are not in the workspace.
Sets someone's out-of-office (`starts_on`, `ends_on`, `delegate`, `note`). Needs `work:delegate` and either `work:reassign` or being their manager.
Clears someone's out-of-office (204). Needs `work:delegate` and either `work:reassign` or being their manager.

areas.name: Files
areas.intro: Resumable uploads, virus scanning, previews and short-lived download links.

routes.summary: The workspace Files view (`file:view_all`), or the caller's own uploads.
Starts a resumable upload from `name`, `size` and optional `content_type` (`file:upload`). 201 with the file and the `chunk_size` to send it in.
routes.exempt: reserves an upload; file.uploaded/quarantined/rejected is appended when it completes

routes.summary: Storage usage for the workspace Files view (`file:view_all`).
Completed files nothing links to, older than `files.orphan_purge_after` (`file:view_all`).
Deletes every orphaned file and returns how many (`file:delete`).
Bulk retention change (E2E-R1-12): sets or clears the class of the chosen files, with a reason.
One file and the records it is linked to, for anyone who may see it (its uploader, `file:view_all`, or a reader of what it is attached to); otherwise 404.
Deletes a file (204). Uploaders may delete their own unattached files; anything else needs `file:delete`. Your own file attached to a record without it is 409 `file_linked`.
One chunk at `offset` (raw bytes). Resume by reading `received` from `GET /files/{id}`.
routes.exempt: chunk transfer of the caller's own upload; audited at completion

routes.summary: Finishes the caller's own upload once every byte has arrived; the file is hashed, type-sniffed and scanned. 409 when the upload is not open or bytes are still missing.
A signed, single-member download link valid for 5 minutes.
A signed preview link for a clean previewable file (`kind: image|pdf|docx|xlsx|csv`), or `kind: none` and no URL. Same permission rules as `download-url`.
Attaches a file the caller can see to a draft document version (`object_type: artifact_version`, `object_id`); needs `edit_draft` on its kind. 204; 409 past draft.
Detaches a file from a draft document version (`edit_draft` on its kind). 204; 409 once the version is past draft.
Files attached to a document version (readers of the version see them).
Serves a file for a valid token; re-checks membership, permission and file state every time.
Serves a previewable file for a valid preview token, re-authorized on every request, under a strict sandboxing CSP. Anything not on the preview allow-list is 415.

areas.name: Notifications
areas.intro: Your in-app notifications and how you are notified.

routes.summary: Your in-app notifications, newest first, with the unread count. Query: `unread=true` for unread only, `limit` (default 50).
Marks all your notifications read; returns how many were marked.
routes.exempt: personal read state of the caller's own inbox; no security or business effect

routes.summary: Marks one of your notifications read (204).
routes.exempt: personal read state of the caller's own inbox; no security or business effect

routes.summary: Your delivery preferences (digests, quiet hours), with your overrides applied over the workspace defaults.
Replaces the caller's overrides; `null` fields follow the workspace defaults. Audited.

areas.name: Profile
areas.intro: Your name, time zone and language.

routes.summary: Your email, display name, time zone and language, plus the languages offered. Shared by every workspace you belong to.
Changes any of `display_name`, `timezone` (IANA name) and `locale`; omitted fields are kept. 422 for an invalid value. Audited; returns the updated profile.

areas.name: Saved views and exports
areas.intro: Saved table views (personal, shared, by role) and recorded CSV and XLSX exports.

routes.summary: My views and the views shared with me for a list (mine first, then by name).
Saves a view of a list (`list`, `name`, `state`), private or shared with everyone (`shared`) or one role (`shared_role`); `is_default` makes it your default for that list. 201.
The roles a view can be shared with.
Only the owner changes a view (shared views included).
Deletes one of your saved views (204). 403 for a shared view you don't own.

Records that the member exported a grid view. CSV: the browser builds the file from rows it was already allowed to see, and gets 204. XLSX: the browser sends exactly those cells and gets the workbook back; text cells stay text (no formulas).

areas.name: Settings
areas.intro: Workspace settings with layered defaults, department overrides, floors and configuration profiles.

routes.summary: The workspace look for every member: the accent with its contrast-safe shades, the default theme, the logo and the effective terminology (every term, workspace label or product default). Readable without settings permissions: it is what the UI paints.
Renames the workspace (owners and admins: `workspace:settings.manage`). Recorded on the workspace chain, and on the system chain by the platform service.
The workspace logo for every member: the image bytes (metadata stripped, as previews), served inline only as an image, never sniffed, never cached across workspaces.
The effective value of every workspace setting (`workspace:settings.view`).
The explainer: final value and every contributing layer.
One setting's effective value and the layers behind it, with its revision as the ETag (`workspace:settings.view`); 404 for an unknown key.
Sets a workspace setting (`value`, optional `reason`) under the key's own permission (some also need step-up); optional `If-Match: "<revision>"` (412 if stale), 422 if invalid.
The last 100 changes to one setting, newest first (`workspace:settings.view`).
Department-scopable keys resolved for one department, with its own overrides.
Sets a department override (`value`, optional `reason`) under the key's permission on that department; optional `If-Match` (412 if stale), 422 if not scopable.
Removes a department's override so the workspace value applies again; optional `If-Match` (412 if stale), 404 if there is no override.
Preview of a profile switch: every key that would change. The ETag is the plan basis.
Applies the plan whose basis is in `If-Match` (required): step-up, a reason, and the permission of every key it changes. One audit event (`settings.profile_switched`).

areas.name: Audit trail
areas.intro: The hash-chained audit trail: search events, object timelines, chain verification, saved queries and exports.

routes.summary: Audit events filtered by time, `actor` or `member`, action, category, object and result, in keyset pages (`page[size]`, `page[cursor]`). `audit:view` sees the workspace chain; `audit:view_own` sees only the caller's own events.
Every event for one object, oldest first. `artifact` spans all of the artifact's versions (the library records lifecycle events per version).
Recomputes the workspace chain and reports the first sequence that does not verify.
The caller's saved audit queries. Needs `audit:view` or `audit:view_own`.
Saves a named set of audit `filters` for the caller; 201. Needs `audit:view` or `audit:view_own`.
Deletes one of the caller's saved audit queries; 204 (404 if not theirs). Needs `audit:view` or `audit:view_own`.
The caller's background exports, newest first.
Synchronous export of up to 10 000 events (newest first). `Procera-Export-Truncated: true` means more matched; narrow the filters. Larger exports move to the export job later.
The state of one of the caller's background audit exports (rows, file, error). Needs `audit:export`; 404 for anyone else's.
`POST /audit/query`: AND/OR filter tree, sorted on the chain, keyset pages.
routes.exempt: read-only query; POST only carries the structured filter body

areas.name: Encryption keys
areas.intro: The workspace's encryption keys and their rotation.

routes.summary: The active key version, every key version with how many values it still wraps, and how many await rewrap. Needs `workspace:settings.view`.
Rotates to a new key version; existing values are rewrapped in the background. Needs `workspace:settings.manage`, a recent sign-in and a `reason` (422 if empty).

areas.name: Templates
areas.intro: The template gallery.

routes.summary: The packs, what each creates and, for members who may install it, which of its documents already exist in the workspace (by key).

Creates a pack's documents as drafts (`documents` to pick some, `on_conflict` `skip` or `copy`, `campaign` for a suggested plan). 201 when anything was created. Needs `template:install` and `<kind>:create` for each kind installed.

areas.name: Password recovery
areas.intro: Forgotten passwords, reset links, changing your password and admin account controls.

routes.summary: Always 202 with the same body, whether or not the account exists (no enumeration). The email is queued in the background so the answer takes the same time either way.
Whether a reset link still works, so the page can say so before the person types a password.
Sets a new password from a reset link (`token`, `password`); 204, and the account owner is emailed. An invalid, expired or used link is refused with 400. Rate-limited per IP.
After `password_change_required`: sets the new password and continues the sign-in (two-step verification next when the account has it).
Account › Security: change the password. Other sessions end; this one continues with the returned access token.
Emails the member a password reset link. Needs `member:security.manage` on the member, a recent step-up and a `reason`; 204, 409 if deactivated.
Makes the member choose a new password at next sign-in (`member:security.manage`, step-up, `reason`); 204. 409 if deactivated or used in other workspaces.
Ends all of the member's sessions (`member:security.manage`, step-up, `reason`); 204. 409 if deactivated or used in other workspaces.
Removes the member's two-step verification (`member:security.manage`, step-up, `reason`); 204. 409 if deactivated or used in other workspaces.

areas.name: System plane: workspaces
areas.intro: For system administrators: create, rename, suspend, restore and schedule deletion of workspaces, and quotas. Never reads workspace content.

routes.summary: One-time creation of the first system owner from the bootstrap `token`, with `email`, `display_name` and `password` (201). 401 for a bad or used token, 409 once bootstrapped.
Your user id and system roles. Like every system route, needs a system role and MFA.
The console's workspace grid (`?state=&profile=&q=`): metadata, quotas and usage counts.
Creates a workspace (201, with `Location` and `ETag`); 409 if the slug is taken. Needs `system.owner` or `system.admin`.
One workspace with its quotas and usage counts, as the console lists it, with an `ETag` of its revision. Any system role.
Renames a workspace (`name`). Honours `If-Match` (412 when stale). Needs `system.owner` or `system.admin`.
Suspends a workspace, `mode` `read_only` or `locked`, with a `reason`. Needs `system.owner`/`system.admin` and a recent sign-in; `If-Match` honoured (412).
Returns a suspended or deletion-scheduled workspace to active (409 otherwise). Needs `system.owner`/`system.admin` and a recent sign-in; `If-Match` honoured (412).
Schedules deletion after `grace_days`, with a `reason`. Needs `system.owner`/`system.admin` and a recent sign-in; `If-Match` honoured (412).
Replaces a workspace's quotas; returns the workspace with usage. Needs `system.owner` or `system.admin` and a recent sign-in.
A fresh one-time link to the owner's pending invitation (for when email isn't set up). Handing over a credential needs a recent authentication; the earlier link stops working.
The platform floors every workspace's settings are held to. Any system role.

Sets a platform floor. Raising it never rewrites workspace values; looser ones resolve as clamped. Floors bind every workspace's security, so this needs a recent authentication (step-up) and, when `If-Match` carries the listed revision, refuses a stale edit (412).

areas.name: System plane: console
areas.intro: For system administrators: platform health and configuration.

routes.summary: The quota bundle each configuration profile starts with. Any system role.
Replaces one profile's default quotas for new workspaces. Needs `system.owner` or `system.admin` and a recent sign-in; `If-Match` honoured (412).
Platform health. `status` is `ok`, `degraded` (something needs a look) or `down`.
The system chain through the shared explorer, newest first. System administrators' names are resolved; every other actor keeps its pseudonymous subject reference.
Recomputes the system chain and reports the first sequence that does not verify.

areas.name: System plane: email
areas.intro: For system administrators: the outgoing email (SMTP) settings.

routes.summary: The email relay in use (`source`: environment, database or none), the stored settings without the password, and the mail queue, with an `ETag`. Needs owner, admin or auditor.
Saves the SMTP relay settings. Requires `If-Match` (428 without; `"0"` when none stored), a recent sign-in and `system.owner`/`system.admin`; 409 when set by the environment.
Sends one test message to `to` through the relay in use and returns whether it was sent (or a safe error category); audited either way. 409 if email is not set up.
Read-only deployment facts: nothing here is configurable from the console yet.

areas.name: Signing
areas.intro: Employee e-signing: envelopes from a PDF, recipients, fields, send and void for senders (`document:send_for_signature`; everyone's with `document:view_all`, voiding anyone's with `document:void`), and the signing ceremony for recipients: open it, sign (consent, a typed or drawn signature, their fields) or decline. `strong` envelopes need a recent sign-in to sign. API tokens never reach `/signing/*`. The document is served from here.

routes.summary: Envelopes I sent (default), or every envelope with `document:view_all`; newest first, at most 500, without fields.

A draft envelope for an uploaded, clean PDF (`title`, optional `message`, `file_id`, `order` sequential|parallel, `mode` simple|strong, `expires_in_days` 1–365, default 30, `bulk` to send a copy to each person in a group; `document:send_for_signature`). 201 with the envelope; 422 for a PDF that can't be signed.
An envelope with its recipients and fields, for its sender, its recipients (once sent) or `document:view_all`.
Replaces a draft's recipients in signing order (`[{membership_id, role: signer|cc}]`, at most 50, active members). Honours `If-Match`.

Replaces a draft's fields (`kind` signature|initials|date_signed| name|text|checkbox, `recipient_id` of a signer, `page`, `x`/`y`/`w`/`h` as fractions of the page from its top-left corner, `required`, `label`). Honours `If-Match`.
Sends a draft (every signer needs a signature field); the document and fields are frozen and the signers whose turn it is are notified. Honours `If-Match`.
Cancels a sent envelope with a `reason` (its sender, or anyone with `document:void`); signers who were asked are told.

Sends a bulk draft to everyone in `audience` (`all`, `departments`, `groups`, `roles`, `locations`): one copy each, signed by that person, grouped in a batch (at most 2,000 people). Honours `If-Match`. 201 with the batch.
Reminds the signer whose turn it is now (its sender; at most once an hour per signer). Returns `{reminded}`.
Group sends I made (or everyone's with `document:view_all`), newest first, with their counts.
A group send with each person's progress (its sender or `document:view_all`): `counts {total, signed, waiting, viewed, declined, cancelled, expired}`, `rows`.
Reminds everyone in a group send who hasn't signed yet (its sender; at most once an hour each). Returns `{reminded}`.
Cancels every copy still waiting for a signature, with a `reason` (its sender, or `document:void`). Returns `{cancelled}`.
The PDF (`application/pdf`): the original the signers review, or the signed copy with its certificate once everyone has signed (409 before).
The envelopes I'm on: `to_sign` when it's my turn, then the rest (waiting, signed, declined, completed copies).
The signing ceremony for my recipient row: the envelope, my fields, whether it's my turn, everyone's progress, and the consent text. The first open is recorded.

Signs on my turn with `document_hash` (the one shown), `consent: true`, `adopted {kind: typed|drawn, text, image?}` and `values` for my text and checkbox fields. `strong` envelopes need a recent sign-in (401 `step_up_required`). The last signature completes the envelope.
Declines with a `reason`; the envelope ends for everyone and the sender is told.
